title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: A graph drawn on the torus is critical for 5-choosability if and only if it is $6$-critical.
context_text: A list assignment $L$ gives each vertex a set of colours; it is a $k$-list assignment if all lists have size at least $k$, and an $L$-colouring is a proper colouring with each vertex coloured from its list. $G$ is $k$-choosable if it has an $L$-colouring for every $k$-list assignment $L$. $G$ is critical for $k$-choosability if it is not $k$-choosable but every proper subgraph is; it is critical for $k$-list colouring if for some $k$-list assignment $L$ it has no $L$-colouring but every proper subgraph has one; it is $k$-critical if it is a minimal graph of chromatic number at least $k$. Thomassen proved that exactly four 6-critical graphs embed on the torus, so these characterise 5-colourability of toroidal graphs; Postle proved that 5-choosability on any fixed surface is characterised by finitely many minimal obstructions, but explicit lists are known only for the sphere (none) and the projective plane ($K_6$ only), and it is unknown whether the torus has any obstruction to 5-choosability beyond the four 6-critical graphs. A non-contractible triangle is a triangle forming a non-contractible curve; a cyclic system of non-contractible triangles is a cyclic sequence of distinct, pairwise homotopic (laminar) non-contractible triangles $C_1,\dots,C_m$ such that, for each $i$ (with $C_{m+1}=C_1$), some cylindrical region of the torus between $C_i$ and $C_{i+1}$ contains no other triangle of the system; its spacing is the maximum, over these $m$ regions (cut open into a cylinder), of the distance between their two boundary triangles. The authors prove by computer-assisted enumeration that a toroidal graph containing a cyclic system of non-contractible triangles of spacing at most four is critical for 5-choosability iff it is one of Thomassen's four 6-critical graphs ($K_7$ being the only such graph critical for 5-list colouring but not for 5-choosability). The conjecture says that the cyclic-system assumption can be dropped. It is equivalent to the statement that a toroidal graph is 5-choosable if and only if it is 5-colourable.
paper_title: Towards Characterization of 5-List-Colorability of Toroidal Graphs

title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: A toroidal graph is $5$-choosable if and only if it is $5$-colorable.
context_text: A list assignment $L$ gives each vertex a set of colours; it is a $k$-list assignment if all lists have size at least $k$, and an $L$-colouring is a proper colouring with each vertex coloured from its list. $G$ is $k$-choosable if it has an $L$-colouring for every $k$-list assignment $L$. $G$ is critical for $k$-choosability if it is not $k$-choosable but every proper subgraph is; it is critical for $k$-list colouring if for some $k$-list assignment $L$ it has no $L$-colouring but every proper subgraph has one; it is $k$-critical if it is a minimal graph of chromatic number at least $k$. A non-contractible triangle is a triangle forming a non-contractible curve; a cyclic system of non-contractible triangles is a cyclic sequence of distinct, pairwise homotopic (laminar) non-contractible triangles $C_1,\dots,C_m$ such that, for each $i$ (with $C_{m+1}=C_1$), some cylindrical region of the torus between $C_i$ and $C_{i+1}$ contains no other triangle of the system; its spacing is the maximum, over these $m$ regions (cut open into a cylinder), of the distance between their two boundary triangles. The conjecture is equivalent to the statement that a graph drawn on the torus is critical for 5-choosability if and only if it is 6-critical, i.e. that the only minimal obstructions to 5-choosability on the torus are Thomassen's four 6-critical graphs; it would be a choosability analogue of Thomassen's characterisation of 5-colourability on the torus.

title: Conjecture 4
statement_text: Every graph drawn on the torus with edge-width at least four is 5-choosable.
context_text: A list assignment $L$ gives each vertex a set of colours; it is a $k$-list assignment if all lists have size at least $k$, and an $L$-colouring is a proper colouring with each vertex coloured from its list. $G$ is $k$-choosable if it has an $L$-colouring for every $k$-list assignment $L$. $G$ is critical for $k$-choosability if it is not $k$-choosable but every proper subgraph is; it is critical for $k$-list colouring if for some $k$-list assignment $L$ it has no $L$-colouring but every proper subgraph has one; it is $k$-critical if it is a minimal graph of chromatic number at least $k$. The edge-width of a graph drawn on a surface is the length of its shortest non-contractible cycle; edge-width at least four means in particular no non-contractible triangles. The authors conjecture that a toroidal graph is 5-choosable iff it is 5-colourable, and prove it for graphs containing a cyclic system of non-contractible triangles of spacing at most four; graphs of edge-width at least four are the complementary case, and this conjecture would be an important step. Postle proved that the edge-width of a graph critical for 5-list colouring is at most logarithmic in its genus, so the conjecture holds with four replaced by a sufficiently large constant.
paper_title: Towards Characterization of 5-List-Colorability of Toroidal Graphs

title: Conjecture 8
statement_text: There is no critical prism-canvas of spacing at least five.
context_text: A list assignment $L$ gives each vertex a set of colours, and an $L$-colouring is a proper colouring from the lists. For a subgraph $T$ of $G$, $G$ is $T$-critical with respect to $L$ if $G\neq T$ and for every proper subgraph $G'\supseteq T$ some $L$-colouring of $T$ extends to $G'$ but not to $G$. A prism-canvas $(F,T_1,T_2,L)$ consists of a connected graph $F$ drawn on the sphere with two distinct faces bounded by triangles $T_1,T_2$ (equivalently, drawn in a cylinder with $T_1,T_2$ as boundaries) and a list assignment with $|L(v)|\ge5$ for every $v\notin V(T_1\cup T_2)$; it is critical if $F$ is $(T_1\cup T_2)$-critical with respect to $L$, and its spacing is the distance between $T_1$ and $T_2$ in $F$. Postle proved that there is an integer $D$ such that every critical prism-canvas has spacing less than $D$ (i.e. for spacing at least $D$ every $L$-colouring of $T_1\cup T_2$ extends to $F$); his $D$ is not explicit, roughly 100. Every critical prism-canvas is obtained from its skeleton ($T_1\cup T_2$ plus a shortest path between them) by pasting chordless critical cycle-canvases (5-list-assigned disk drawings that are critical with respect to their boundary cycle) of circumference at most $2d+6$ into its faces. Using an enumeration of chordless critical cycle-canvases of circumference at most 14, the authors obtained 510, 2719, 300 and 5 candidates for critical prism-canvases of spacing 1, 2, 3 and 4; the rapid decrease suggests $D=5$, which is the conjecture. Such canvases are the building blocks of toroidal graphs critical for 5-list colouring.
paper_title: Towards Characterization of 5-List-Colorability of Toroidal Graphs
